holidays.name: World Smile Day (First Friday of October)
holidays.description: A day dedicated to doing acts of kindness and helping at least one person smile. Expect plenty of yellow, grinning faces and cheerful strangers.
holidays.origin: Created by commercial artist Harvey Ball, who designed the iconic Smiley Face in 1963. He founded World Smile Day in 1999 to keep the symbol from being overly commercialized. It is held on the first Friday of October, so it sometimes lands on October 2.
holidays.funFact: Harvey Ball was paid just $45 for creating the Smiley Face and never trademarked it.

holidays.name: National Fried Scallops Day
holidays.description: A day for seafood lovers to celebrate crispy, golden fried scallops, whether they are served at a seaside shack or made at home.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that appears on food-observance calendars, celebrating the popular fried seafood dish of coastal communities, especially in New England.
holidays.funFact: Scallops are one of the few bivalves that can swim, clapping their shells together to jet through the water, and some species have up to 200 tiny blue eyes.

holidays.name: National Custodial Worker Day
holidays.description: A salute to the janitors and custodians who keep schools, offices, and public buildings clean and running smoothly, often unnoticed.
holidays.origin: Observed on October 2 in the United States as a way to recognize the essential work of custodial staff, who are often behind the scenes.
holidays.funFact: Custodians are often the first to arrive and last to leave a building, and many hold keys to practically every door in it.

holidays.name: International Day of Non-Violence
holidays.description: A global day promoting peace, tolerance, understanding, and nonviolence through education and public awareness.
holidays.origin: The United Nations established it in 2007 on Gandhi's birthday, October 2, to honor the leader of India's nonviolent independence movement and promote his philosophy worldwide.
holidays.funFact: Gandhi was nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize several times but never won it.

holidays.name: Name Your Car Day
holidays.description: A day to give your trusty vehicle a proper name, whether it's Herbie, Betsy, or Sir Rusts-a-Lot, and finally acknowledge it as part of the family.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, pop-culture-style holiday celebrated by car owners who treat their vehicles like beloved pets. Many calendars place it on October 2.
holidays.funFact: Surveys have repeatedly found that a large share of drivers have named their cars, with many saying the name fits the vehicle's personality.
